The test image shows a split soybean stem with **white/light gray pith** internally. Key observations:
- Stem split lengthwise
- Internal pith is predominantly white/light colored
- Some dark streaking in vascular tissue
- Dry, bleached external stem appearance

Now let me check the part index and then view reference images.

The image shows a **split soybean stem** with white/light gray pith internally. This narrows to stem candidates: Anthracnose, Brown_Stem_Rot, Charcoal_Rot, Fusarium, Green_stem_disorder, Phytophthora, Pythium_damping_off, Rhizoctonia, Tobacco_Streak_Virus, White_Mold. Also noting SDS is characterized by white pith when stems are cut.

Key feature: **white pith** (not brown). This immediately differentiates from Brown_Stem_Rot (brown pith) and points toward SDS or White_Mold.

Let me check White_Mold stem first:
White Mold shows fluffy white mycelium and black sclerotia - not matching. Now checking Charcoal Rot stem:
This shows external stem surface. Let me check the other Charcoal Rot stem image which shows internal structure:

This Charcoal Rot reference (split stems with white pith and black dotted microsclerotia on external surface) is a very strong visual match to the test image. Let me now check Brown_Stem_Rot to confirm differentiation:
BSR reference shows green stems with white pith (early/healthy looking). The test image shows a dry, mature split stem. Now checking Sudden_death_syndrome:
SDS whole plant shows yellowing foliage - not directly comparable. Let me check Fusarium stem:
Fusarium shows rotted, discolored stems - doesn't match. Now checking Phytophthora stem:
Phytophthora shows external stem canker in field context - not matching. Now checking Rhizoctonia stem:
Rhizoctonia shows reddish-brown basal canker on seedling - not matching. Let me use my last view on Charcoal_Rot whole_plant to further confirm:

Charcoal Rot whole_plant shows wilted, dry plants consistent with late-season disease.

**Summary of analysis:**

- **Test image**: Split soybean stem, white/light gray pith, dark streaking in vascular tissue, dry bleached external stem
- **Charcoal Rot (Soybean_Dise_49.jpg)**: Near-identical pattern — split stems held in hand, white internal pith, dark microsclerotia speckling on external surface. Strong visual match.
- **Brown Stem Rot**: Would show BROWN pith — ruled out
- **White Mold**: Would show fluffy white mycelium and embedded black sclerotia — ruled out
- **Fusarium/Phytophthora/Rhizoctonia**: All show different external lesion patterns — ruled out
- **SDS**: White pith is characteristic, but SDS isn't in the stem category of the part_index and the context (dry, bleached mature stem with grayish external surface) fits Charcoal Rot better

The combination of white pith, dark internal vascular streaking, grayish-charcoal external stem appearance, and near-identical framing to the Charcoal Rot reference image strongly supports Charcoal Rot.
